USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Selecting the monitoring test

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient taking stable long-term warfarin has a new interacting medicine added. The clinician plans additional laboratory monitoring to assess anticoagulant intensity. Which test is conventionally used to guide warfarin dosing in this setting?

  1. Prothrombin time expressed as INR
  2. Bleeding time
  3. Anti-factor Xa activity calibrated to heparin
  4. Platelet count alone
  5. Serum thrombin concentration
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Prothrombin time expressed as INR

INR standardizes prothrombin time for vitamin K antagonist monitoring.

Understanding the options

Prothrombin time expressed as INR
INR standardizes prothrombin time for vitamin K antagonist monitoring.
Bleeding time
Bleeding time is not the dosing test for warfarin.
Anti-factor Xa activity calibrated to heparin
Heparin-calibrated anti-Xa testing measures a different anticoagulant effect.
Platelet count alone
Platelet counts do not quantify vitamin K antagonist intensity.
Serum thrombin concentration
Serum thrombin concentration is not the routine clinical monitoring method.
